description: A lion poured from the volcano's throat. Its obsidian mane cools black; its roar glows through the cracks.
lore: Strike the light, not the dark. That is the whole of what the trade knows about it, and it is a worse rule than it sounds. Cold, the glass is armour: a spear takes a chip out of the mane, skates off, and the animal does not appear to notice it has been hit. The cracks only open when it is roused, so the one part of it that can be worked is the part that is not there until it has decided about you. Finding one is the easy half. Look for a scatter of boulders with nothing growing on any of them.

[[characters/54bead23|Osric]] went up to look on purpose. He still counts in living years, and he had spent all of them at a forge in a country with no mountains in it. He got within thirty feet, sat down on the scree and watched it sleep the afternoon out, black and cold and breathing about once a minute. What he wanted was the heat. He asked about it afterwards, carefully, the way a new smith asks a question he suspects is stupid, and got the trade's answer: it is the hottest thing in the country and the only fire in it you cannot sit at, and you cannot tell it anything either. He has been up three times since. A man arrived here with a working life still in his hands, in a place that needs nothing made, and the one great heat within reach of him is no use to anybody. He has stopped mentioning it at the fire.
gm_notes: The showy one, played practical: the rule (strike the light) is a real tactic that costs you the safe distance, and the bare boulders are the tracking sign. Two paragraphs on purpose — the rule, then the man. Osric carries it: a recently woken tradesman looking for work in a country that does not require any, which is the newly-dead problem in miniature. The heat is deliberately useless; a fire nobody can sit at is the inversion of the Keeping and should stay unexploitable.
